y2-06.recommendedPriorKnowledge: It is required to have a solid background in neuroscience topics and techniques. For example, you need to know the underlying mechanisms of techniques like EEG, MEG, fMRI, or TMS. You need to know the mechanisms of action potential generation, synaptic transmission, or dendritic integration. Knowledge of basic brain anatomy (cortical regions, major subcortical structures) is also required. Upon completion of the courses Introductory Psychology and Brain & Cognition you will have required this knowledge.

components: Work and Organisational Psychology & Social Psychology
Academic-skills practicals and research participation are compulsory without additional credits. All earlier reading and writing assignments must be passed before the first-year thesis.
This pathway completes all 60 first-year credits, including Research Methods & Statistics and research participation, before Year 2. The common courses require 48 or 60 first-year credits.
One coherent Brain and Cognition specialisation is selected. Its four courses require the full first year and Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, completed before this semester.
B&C Toolbox: Experimental and Neuroscientific Methods
The 12-EC toolbox integrates behavioural experiments, neuroscience methods, data analysis, experimental design and Python programming.
Entry requires the full first year, Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, Psychological Research and at least 18 EC of the specialisation, including its toolbox. All are completed in Year 2.

The 12-EC empirical thesis follows the first part of Behavioural Research Toolbox. The earlier requirements and at least 18 specialisation credits must be passed. Five colloquium points must also be obtained; they add no separate degree credits. Students conduct supervised group research and write individual empirical reports.
Current Topics: Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic
Selected from the restricted period-one Current Topics menu: consciousness research through psychological, neuroscientific and clinical approaches.
Selected from the restricted period-two Current Topics menu: the relationship between psychological science and AI. The full first year is required; prior AI or programming knowledge is not.

Thirty EC remain genuinely open for a second specialisation, minor, exchange or an approved coherent course package. findings: Public programme and dated guide confirm a 180-EC research-university Psychology degree. Registry row 443 and recognized code 56604 identify the generic English/Dutch full-time target. The English programme carries the same core and six shared specialisations; Clinical Neuropsychology is an additional Dutch-only option, valid within this bilingual target. No professional registration or treatment entitlement is inferred.

The public page’s introductory prose begins its list with Work and Organisational Psychology, but its detailed numbered curriculum begins with Brain and Cognition; the dated guide likewise lists Brain and Cognition as studyPathId 199 first. Retained the existing neutral detailed-order selection before reconsidering UCR courses. It is not claimed to be a default. The guide confirms its four named courses: Introduction to Neuroscience 6, From Perception to Consciousness 6, Memory/Language/Emotion 6 and Toolbox 12, totalling thirty EC without counting their parent aggregate.

The seven first-year credit-bearing components total sixty. Practicals Academic Skills and Research Participation are explicitly zero-credit mandatory requirements. Reading/Writing of Scientific Texts assignments in the first semester must pass before second-semester continuation; all earlier assignments must pass before the first-year thesis. The pathway completes them in order. The forty-eight-credit BSA is met by the complete sixty-credit first year.

The four common Year-2 components total thirty. Scientific/Statistical Reasoning requires forty-eight first-year EC including Research Methods/Statistics; Psychological Communication and Fundamentals require forty-eight. Psychological Research requires all sixty including research participation. Completing the full first year meets all thresholds. The four selected Brain and Cognition courses then require the full first year including participation plus Scientific/Statistical Reasoning, which finishes in Year-2 period two before the specialisation begins in period four.

Behavioural Research Toolbox is the named six-credit Year-3 methods course for Brain and Cognition. It runs in period one and requires the full first year, Scientific/Statistical Reasoning, Psychological Research and at least eighteen specialisation credits including its twelve-credit Toolbox. All thirty specialisation credits are completed in Year 2. The twelve-credit Brain and Cognition thesis runs in periods two and three and requires the first part of the Year-3 Toolbox plus the earlier requirements and at least eighteen specialisation credits. This order is valid; the thesis is one empirical group project with individual analysis and article, not a generic unrestricted dissertation.

Five colloquium points must be completed and are recorded as a thesis partial grade. They can be collected from Year 1 and are mandatory without separately credited EC. They are explicitly retained along with zero-credit practicals and participation.

Instantiated both restricted Current Topics choices before UCR reassessment: Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic is offered in period one and Psychology and AI in period two. Both are in the dated shared choice menus and require sixty first-year credits including research participation; no prior AI/programming course is mandatory. The topics coherently extend the selected cognitive/neuroscience route. Current Topics plus methods and thesis comprise thirty EC; no menu alternatives are summed.

The final thirty-credit optional profile remains genuinely open to a second specialisation, minor, exchange or an individually approved coherent package. The dated elective page requires Examination Board approval for individual packages, research-university level, no Psychology overlap and no more than twelve first-year EC. External minors need approval. No named host, minor or elective is invented. Credits total sixty per year and 180 uniquely; the public prospective page is not used to override dated course entry rules. There is no material unresolved curriculum conflict requiring an additional OER source.

All nineteen selected credit-bearing entries plus the two zero-credit requirements were inspected for contents, credits, periods and entry rules. In particular Psychological Communication is interviewing/listening practice, Psychological Research includes test construction and a scientific article, the specialisation Toolbox includes neural measurement and Python experiments, and Behavioural Research Toolbox includes simulation/model fitting and PsychoPy. These specifics govern the deliberately partial UCR relationships.
